vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ragflow-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is a well-structured integration for the RAGFlow API, providing scripts for dataset management, document ingestion, and retrieval. All network operations are performed using the Python standard library (urllib) and are restricted to the user-defined RAGFLOW_BASE_URL. The SKILL.md instructions include explicit safety requirements, such as mandatory user confirmation before executing deletion commands, and there is no evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions require and read RAGFlow API credentials and repo .env files, but the registry metadata doesn't declare any required environment variables or credentials — this mismatch and the skill's ability to read local files and upload them to an HTTP endpoint deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a RAGFlow dataset/retrieval helper and the included scripts clearly call a RAGFlow HTTP API and require an API key (RAGFLOW_API_KEY / require_api_key) and a base URL (RAGFLOW_BASE_URL / HOST_ADDRESS / CLI flag). However the registry metadata declares no required env vars or primary credential. Requesting an API key is legitimate for this purpose, but the published metadata omits these required credentials, which is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the bundled scripts and to upload local files (explicit local paths or drag-and-drop). The scripts will read repository .env files and environment variables, and then send files and requests to whatever base_url is resolved. The instructions do not call out the need for an API key or .env, nor do they warn that local files and .env contents will be read and transmitted — this broad access is not fully documented in the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction-and-scripts only and does not download or execute third-party installers. That lowers install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code requires secrets (RAGFLOW_API_KEY) and may use env variables for base URL (RAGFLOW_BASE_URL, RAGFLOW_API_URL, HOST_ADDRESS). The registry metadata did not declare these environment requirements. Also scripts load the repository .env file and inject variables into the environment, which can surface other local secrets unexpectedly. Asking for an API key is expected for the stated purpose, but the omission in metadata and the .env loading increase the chance of accidental exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent inclusion (always: false) and there is no install-time modification of other skills or system-wide configuration evident in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package contains a set of scripts that interact with a RAGFlow HTTP API and will: (1) read repository .env files and environment variables, (2) require an API key (RAGFLOW_API_KEY) and a base URL (RAGFLOW_BASE_URL / HOST_ADDRESS or CLI flag), and (3) upload local files to the configured HTTP endpoint. The registry entry failing to declare required environment variables is the main red flag — verify before installing. Before you proceed: 1) Confirm you will provide a limited-scope RAGFlow API key (not broad cloud credentials). 2) Verify the base_url the scripts will use (avoid unintentionally pointing to an untrusted remote server). 3) Be aware that local file paths you supply (and any secrets in a repository .env) may be read and sent to the server. 4) If you need stronger assurance, ask the publisher to update the metadata to list required env vars (RAGFLOW_API_KEY, RAGFLOW_BASE_URL/HOST_ADDRESS) and review the full scripts locally to confirm behavior. If you cannot verify those points, treat installation as risky.
